threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Dalston Junction' instead of just 'Junction' when chatting with mates in the local pubs.
Last night on the 59, a couple debated loudly whether the driver was a wizard. They thought he disappeared after one stop. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a couple arguing loudly over who had the best döner in the middle of Hermannplatz. Classic Neukölln chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a streed vendor selling currywurst with vegan sauce at 3 AM, surrounded by a circle of late-night techno enthusiasts.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their calm during a BART breakdown—while newcomers are panicking, we’re already texting our backup bus routes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 this morning; a guy serenaded the entire bus with a ukulele. Only in SF would a chilly commute turn into an impromptu concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell, but it's the little plazas here, like Plaça del Sol, where the real vibe lives. They miss the heart of Gràcia.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new if they still call it 'Las Ramblas' instead of just 'Rambles'—it's a small but telling slip.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to stand on the right on the escalators. Watch out for the looks from the locals!
Saw a guy on the 133 last night trying to barter with a busker. They settled on a handful of change for a rendition of 'Wonderwall'. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Standing in line at the Döner place on Weserstraße, I realized everyone was debating the best last stop for a night out—only in Neukölln does that feel like community.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you'll find spontaneous street concerts breaking out, often led by a random accordion player. It's like a free music festival every weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they react when BART breaks down—they roll their eyes and pull out a book, not the panic I see from tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a dog lounging on the tracks at Civic Center, a Muni classic. The way commuters just shrugged and waited? So SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they’ll find a quiet haven in Gràcia, but on match days, it’s a rowdy festival of Barça fans. Totally different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle with the 'Gràcia' pronunciation; they say 'Graa-sia' instead of 'Grat-zi-a'.
